commands.name: harness_saturation_tiny_ring
commands.stderr_excerpt: harness[saturation]: passed — saturation-detected-no-critical-loss: tiny ring (4096 B) shed 2385 of 2400 oracle events; loss reconciled by independent oracle (never a false zero)

assertions: task-53: CONFIRMED for the process-lifecycle sensor runtime path — all four user-binding expected outcomes achieved live in a privileged Docker container (--privileged --pid=host) on kernel 7.1.3-2-cachyos: programs loaded+attached, fork/exec/exit ordering proven, saturation drops non-zero and reconciled, supported-load envelope zero-loss at 99.6% of the declared rate. Four secondary sensors (network/dns/syscall/lsm) are BLOCKED at load by pre-existing source-level defects (exact libbpf/verifier errors recorded in commands); they compile cleanly but do not load on this kernel/libbpf and re-open on their owning tasks (13/14/15/33).

BPF sensor programs loaded and attached in a privileged container: bpftool prog loadall accepted process.bpf.o (4 programs: 3 raw_tracepoint + 1 kprobe), file.bpf.o, identity.bpf.o (all rc=0); harness-attached instance verified mid-run via bpftool prog list (ids 24370-24373) and bpftool link list (links 118-121: raw_tracepoint sched_process_fork/exec/exit + kprobe __x64_sys_execve).

Process fork/exec/exit events captured with correct ordering: ordering mode — 100/100 oracle children observed with all four events (fork, exec-kprobe, exec-raw-tp, exit), 0 ordering violations (fork.ts <= exec_kp.ts <= exec.ts <= exit.ts per child), 0 per-CPU seq violations.

Ring buffer saturation produces non-zero drop counters: 4096-byte ring (schema tiny_ring_size_bytes), paused consumer, 600-child flood (2400 oracle events) — reserve_failure_delta=2385 (non-zero), gap_children=597, 577 events consumed; loss reconciled by the independent fork/exec oracle: expected-matched==drops exactly (never a false zero).

Supported-load envelope verified: at 996.4 measured events/s/cpu against the declared 1000 events/s/cpu (bench/schemas/supported-load.v1.json#default_rate_events_per_sec_per_cpu), 37500/37500 oracle children complete, 150000/150000 oracle events matched, reserve_failure_delta=0 — zero critical fixture loss; 256KiB production ring, one deadline-pinned worker per CPU, SCHED_FIFO(10) consumer on dedicated CPU 0.

Accounting honesty proven by counter-example: intermediate runs under heavy host load (load average 70-160 from co-tenant sessions) produced 1-2 transient kernel-side drops per 12000-160000 events; the independent oracle detected every one (verdict=failed, reserve_failure_delta>0) — loss is never claimed from agent counters alone, and a contaminated run was never passed off as the envelope proof.

No BPF programs left pinned after testing: /sys/fs/bpf contains no task53_* entries post-run (NO_TASK53_PINS); harness links are fd-bound and destroyed on process exit (verified: 0 task53-related programs in bpftool prog list after the run).
All 7 sensor objects compile cleanly with clang -target bpf -D__TARGET_ARCH_x86 (rc=0 each); .BTF/.BTF.ext sections present in process.bpf.o.
